MCPToolProvider~inference.name: inference_tool_provider
MCPToolProvider~inference.description: Task-scoped set for inferring a metamodel from sample payloads and handing it to the model atlas: discover the family and its conventions, author the package, validate it against the samples, register and publish. Deliberately omits instance manipulation, import/replay, operations and generics

HttpMCPServerComponent~inference.server.name: osgi-emf-inference-mcp-server
HttpMCPServerComponent~inference.server.instructions: Use this MCP server to infer an Ecore metamodel from sample payloads and hand it to this runtime's model atlas. DISCOVER FIRST: an unknown payload is usually a variant of a model that already exists, so start with list_annotation_sources (the annotation vocabularies of this runtime), then find_classes_by_annotation / find_features_by_annotation - OMIT 'value' to match any value for a key, which is how you locate a model family and check whether a discriminator value is still free. describe_eclass is the read to reach for: it reports one class's EAnnotations in their exact source and key spelling (ExtendedMetaData wire names included), its declared 'superTypes' against inherited 'allSuperTypes' both as <nsURI>#//<Name>, and 'inherited'/'declaringClass' per feature - and it describes abstract classes and interfaces, which is where a family's conventions usually live. Read the two or three classes you are copying from rather than pulling a whole package: export_package emits one registered package's entire .ecore and is for when you want the document itself. list_metamodel gives the index, describe_aspects reads one element's parsed provider metadata. AUTHOR: create_dataset, then ONE create_epackage carrying the whole package in its 'eClassifiers' array - each classifier nests its own eAttributes / eReferences / eAnnotations, an EEnum its eLiterals, and classifiers may reference each other as '#//<Name>' in any declaration order. Do not issue one call per element: the call returns the objectId of every nested element, and add_eclass (which also takes nested eAttributes / eReferences / eAnnotations), add_eattribute, add_ereference, add_eannotation and modify_feature are for adding to or correcting a package that already exists. Type references are <nsURI>#//<Name> (e.g. http://www.eclipse.org/emf/2002/Ecore#//EString). Follow the conventions of the sibling models you found rather than inventing your own. VALIDATE: create_from_json builds an instance from one sample and tells you itself what did not land - its 'coverage' report names every key of the sample that matched no feature ('unmatchedPaths') and every key whose feature stayed empty ('droppedPaths'). Load EVERY sample and read that report: 'complete': true means the model covers the sample, a non-empty 'unmatchedPaths' means you are missing a feature the payload carries - add it and reload. Pass strict=true to have the call refuse instead of reporting. Do NOT export the XMI to check this - the coverage report is the check, and this set serves no dataset export. PUBLISH: register_package makes the package instantiable and is the precondition for post_to_model_atlas, which hands it to the atlas by nsURI - you never handle the document. Scope, stage and overwrite are fixed by the deployment; only allow-listed namespaces can be registered or published.
